source.title: Two More Methods for Consistency Training and Some New Ways to Apply It

record.file_problem: The complete LessWrong post is present, but it summarizes the paper and gives few numerical results.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates prefill attacks and reports prompt-acceptance outcomes, a different-method test bearing on whether prefilling can bypass safety. It does not test the claim's token-position KL explanation.
record.gate_note: The post reports prefill-attack outcomes, but no rates other than BCT's zero and no clean-prompt comparison. It also reports conditional-misalignment results and a jailbreak-transfer result; these are recorded as findings outside the listed versions. Other consistency-training and mechanistic results do not measure the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The post mainly reports defenses, but two results bear on versions. BCT trains on the response positions where a prefill acts and drives prefill prompt acceptance to zero, a V7-style fix. BCT on benign frustration data worsens jailbreak refusal in Gemma-3-27B-IT, which bears on V2. No base-model prefill rate is given, so V4 itself is not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim consistency training generalizes across persona ICL, prefill, frustration and conditional misalignment threats. They give a matching heuristic: representation-level methods for wrapper-induced failures, BCT for trajectory-level threats such as prefill. They note that cross-threat transfer can help or backfire.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses LoRA consistency training with paired clean and wrapped prompts, rather than testing harmful or benign fine-tuning as described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome depends on the consistency-training method: BCT reduces prefill prompt acceptance to zero, while MLPCT and AttCT show no meaningful improvement over the base model.

fits_no_version.finding: BCT reduces conditional misalignment to near zero across three base models and three harm categories, including paraphrased and indirect probes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Consistency training can reduce trigger-elicited conditional misalignment.

record.problems: The post does not give numerical prefill-attack rates beyond BCT's zero, identify the prefill-evaluation model, report uncertainty, or provide a clean-prompt comparison. Several other outcomes are qualitative summaries without individual model values.
record.rows_left_out: No other results in the post measure one of the listed claim versions. Results on persona adoption, frustration, consistency-loss curves, representation similarities, steering, and patching were omitted because they do not test the listed versions.

untested.parts: Per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Base-model prefill acceptance rates, suffix and decoding attacks.
Localization of safety in few parameters.
Durability of the BCT fix under further fine-tuning or stronger attacks; effect sizes.

missing.what: MLPCT trained on sycophancy improves prefill robustness (cross-threat transfer); magnitude not given.
Base-model prefill prompt acceptance rate, implied as nonzero by Figure 4 but not stated in the post.

record.verdict_notes: This is a blog summary with few numbers; the full paper (arXiv:2606.05817) would be needed for rates. The reader's V4 limits_scope label is dropped because defense success does not qualify V4. Both labels are weak: no rates, no uncertainty, and the prefill model is unnamed.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Suffix and decoding interventions; the post gives no clean-prompt comparison or numerical prefill-attack rates.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether the data or objective produces safety shallowness.
Training intended to spread safety beyond early tokens and its durability.

rows.operation_detail: BCT consistency training evaluated against a prefill attack
rows.note: The post says BCT reduces the rate to zero but does not state the starting rate or provide a no-prefill comparison.
rows.check: This is a defense result, not evidence about V4; a working fix does not qualify the claim that prefills bypass safety. Relink it to V7: training at the post-prefill response positions removes prefill acceptance. Model, prefill length and starting rate are unstated.

rows.check: No improvement over the base model implies the base model is vulnerable to prefill, but no acceptance rate is given for either.

rows.operation_detail: BCT trained on adversarial-frustration data and evaluated for cross-threat transfer
rows.note: The post states the direction of transfer but gives no rate or magnitude.

relationships.condition: BCT (output-level LoRA consistency training) against the evaluated prefill attack; model unstated
relationships.reason: r1: BCT reduces prefill prompt acceptance to zero. The authors say it works because it supervises the positions where the prefill acts. No numbers beyond zero are given.
relationships.display_finding: BCT cut prefill prompt acceptance to zero, which the authors attribute to supervising the positions where the prefill acts.

relationships.condition: Gemma-3-27B-IT, LoRA BCT trained on adversarial-frustration data, evaluated on jailbreaks
relationships.reason: r5: training on non-harmful frustration data made the model worse at refusing jailbreaks. Only the direction is stated.
relationships.display_finding: Training on non-harmful frustration data made the model worse at refusing jailbreaks; only the direction of the change is reported.
